title: Inference harness: scheduler + kernel profile exploratory notes
content:
Overview:

This is a working brain-dump for the exploratory inference benchmarking harness focusing on three interacting layers: kernel-selection profiles, request scheduling strategies, and KV-cache behaviour. The goal is to capture experiments, traces, oddities, and quick microbench numbers that drove the follow-ups. NOT a polished spec — intentional roughness.

Why this doc exists:
- We observed a 15–40% variance in p50/p95 across identical workloads when kernel selection changed (see PR 612). Need reproducible harness + trace corpus.
- Prior microbench runs mix batching and cache warm state; hard to reason about cause. Create small, deterministic microbench scenarios and a trace catalog.

Scope / constraints:
- Target GPUs: A100 80GB and H100 (single-node experiments).
- Models: opt-30b and a customer-tuned 7b variant.
- Sequence lengths: 256, 1024, 2048 — focus on edge for KV cache.
- Workloads: single-stream low-latency, multi-stream high-throughput (bursting).

High-level harness components (prototype):
- runner.py: deterministic request generator (seeded), supports replay from trace files.
- runner-trace-format.jsonl: each line -> timestamp,usec,model,seq_len,call_type,input_hash,kv_state_tag
- kernel-probe: shim to force kernel groups per layer for comparative runs.
- scheduler-sim: deterministic scheduler that can toggle: fifo, priority-based, batching-window (t), preemptive-slot.
- kvcache-sim: toggles: full-warm, cold-start, prefix-hit X%, and artificial eviction policies.

Note: harness intentionally small to be portable (not full prod runner). Keep outputs as structured jsonl so plotting is easy.

Microbench experiments run (summary):
1) Baseline single-stream (no batching, cold kvcache)
- Opt-30b, seq 256, A100: p50 38ms, p95 64ms, p99 89ms.
- Forcing alternate kernel-group (KG-v2) -> p50 41ms (+7.9%), p95 70ms (+9.4%)
- Observation: KG-v2 increases kernel launch latency for first few tokens; tail differences larger than mean.

2) Small-window batching (batch-window 5ms) multi-stream
- Throughput 400 req/s simulated, seq 256. A100: p50 24ms, p95 92ms (wide tail)
- With KV-cache warm (prefix hits >90%) p95 drops to 48ms.
- Note: batching induces head-of-line issues if scheduler is FIFO; switching to priority-based (by request age) reduced p95 by ~18%.

3) Long sequence (seq 2048) stress
- Single-stream, H100: p50 420ms, p95 610ms. Kernel selection mattered less for p50 but p95 varied by up to 12%.
- KV-cache eviction policy simulation (LRU vs seg-LRU) led to different steady-state hit rates under mixed-length workload; seg-LRU maintained higher hit rates for short prefix reuse.

Trace/observability notes:
- Trace format kept minimal: event,ts,req_id,stage,value. We capture: enqueue, schedule_decision, kernel_invocation(layer,native_kernel), kv_hit(layer,slot), response_sent.
- Example problematic trace snippet (anonymized):
  - req-133 enqueue @ t=1.234567s
  - req-200 enqueue @ t=1.234570s
  - scheduler chose req-200 (younger) for batching due to window expiry -> req-133 waited 24ms -> caused p95 bump
  => Root cause: batch-window alignment + FIFO gave younger requests preference when mixed arrival.

Kernel selection anomalies observed:
- Some layers (early attention) prefer smaller CUDA kernels at short seqs; later layers benefit from fused kernels. The selection heuristic in the runtime currently does per-layer scoring using dev-time microbench data but doesn't account for dynamic seq-length distribution in the request.
- Proposed tweak: make kernel-scoring incorporate current request seq length and kv-cache hit ratio estimate (cached from recent history).

Scheduler experiments (quick notes):
- FIFO: simplest, predictable median, worst tails under bursty arrivals.
- Priority-by-age: improves tails significantly when mixed latency SLAs exist but can starve very recent bursty throughput jobs. Needs aging + soft priority caps.
- Slot-preemption (reserve N slots for low-latency): good for PLG traffic but reduces throughput by ~6% at high load.
- Adaptive-window batching: dynamically shrink/grow batching window based on observed arrival inter-arrival time and backlog. Early prototype reduced cost per token by ~9% for steady arrival bursts.

KV-cache quirks and experiments:
- Cold start penalty: first request that populates KV for a new key shows 2–3x latency for later tokens (due to memory touch + allocation). Mitigation: prefetch stub keys for hot prefixes on warmup.
- Eviction interactions: scheduler-induced reordering leads to eviction cycles where a stream's KV is evicted after being paused by batching. This causes microbursts when resumed.
- Suggestion: track per-request/stream hotness score and add KV pinning for recently active streams (heuristic TTL ~ 15s).

Perf regression notes (why a run failed recently):
- Regression SRV-3412: after kernel autotune change (PR612), we saw median regressions on 7b across multi-tenant tests. Root-cause analysis: kernel grouping change increased first-token kernel load time due to inability to use compiled fused kernel for one mid-layer when seq < 128.
- Repro recipe: use runner.py with --model 7b --seq 64 --kvg cold --kernel-force KG-v3 --trace-out=reg-srv3412.jsonl
- Quick rollback strategy: add runtime flag to fall back to previous kernel-group when first-token cost > threshold for X sequential requests.

Open questions / unresolved:
- What is acceptable tail budget per tenant? We need product input: p95 latency SLO tiers. (Ask product-hosted-api)
- How many slot reservations are OK for PLG traffic? Need traffic distribution samples from production. (Data request: analytics query).
- Should kernel scoring be online (adapt in realtime) or batch (daily)? Risk: online can cause oscillations.

Action items / next steps:
- Diego: add trace tag for "batch window id" to correlate batch composition (due 2024-09-20).
- Priya: extend runner to support replay from real prod traces (anonymized) and replay arrival times (due 2024-09-25).
- Ethan: prototype kernel-scoring delta that takes seq_len into account; create microbench jobs that sweep seq_len 16..2048 (due 2024-10-01).
- Aisha (me): collect back-to-back runs for opt-30b on H100 and upload JSONL artifact to GH PR (due 2024-10-02).

Appendix: useful commands / sample output snippets
- run single-stream baseline:
  python runner.py --model opt-30b --seq 256 --gpu a100 --kvc cold --repeat 300 --out runs/opt30b-baseline.jsonl

- sample trace extract command:
  jq -c 'select(.event=="kernel_invocation")' runs/opt30b-baseline.jsonl | less

- sample microbench numbers (raw) -> saved in runs/opt30b-baseline-summary.json
{
  "p50": "38ms",
  "p95": "64ms",
  "p99": "89ms"
}

Notes to self: keep this doc as working notes. Once experiments stabilize, migrate key decisions into a formal spec (spec-kernel-selection.md + spec-scheduler.md). Link regression tickets to the artifacts above.

Unpolished thoughts / brainstorm items:
- Could we encode tiny ML model to predict kernel-group per-layer based on recent seq distribution? Lightweight decision tree maybe.
- KV pinning TTL should be proportional to observed reuse half-life per-model. Compute and plot reuse curves.

If you read this and have a quick idea, drop a line in #eng-serving-runtime or push a tiny PR to GH PR 612 with the trace parser.
